name: hcapp_sendDirectMessage
description: Posts to a direct-message thread (E9.F1.S7): an HC.EventMessage row with EventId and KennelId NULL and ThreadId set — the third key HC.trgCreateSeqNum already numbers by. Mirrors hcapp_sendRoomMessage's rowsets so the chat page and the API's push dispatch work unchanged. Auth: HC6.ValidateAppAuth (spNumber 134, @param NULL — a standard token). Permission gate: BOTH HasherFriendMap rows for @threadId must be live — the caller's and the other party's, neither Removed (nobody ended it) and neither with Ignore = 1 (nobody blocking); otherwise 2013 'You can't message <name>.' (errorType 3), naming nobody's reason. Recipients are the OTHER party's devices only, on builds >= HC6.MinBuildForDmPush(); their FriendNotificationPreference on the thread decides: 2 nothing, 3 silent (badge only), anything else visible. Rowsets 1–3 are computed inside a log-and-swallow TRY so push plumbing can never fail an already-committed send. Since 2026-10-13 a resend of an already-stored @messageId by the same sender in the same thread is idempotent: nothing is written, rowset 0 returns the stored message and the push rowsets are empty, so nobody is notified twice (a resend after a lost reply used to hit PK_EventMessage and report a delivered message as unsent).

parameters.name: deviceId
parameters.description: Registered device UUID. Default NULL (ValidateAppAuth then fails gracefully).

parameters.name: accessToken
parameters.description: Short-lived token (standard, device secret; @param NULL). Default NULL.

parameters.name: threadId
parameters.description: The DM thread (HasherFriendMap.ThreadId shared by both rows). Required; NULL → 2010. Not the caller's, or not open → 2013.

parameters.name: messageId
parameters.description: Client-generated message UUID. Required; NULL → 2010. A duplicate id is a PK violation caught by the CATCH (2014) — the insert is not idempotent.

parameters.name: messageContent
parameters.description: Message body. Required; LEN() = 0 → 2010. More than 4,000 UTF-16 code units (the column width) is REFUSED with 2011 rather than truncated; the parameter is MAX for that reason.

parameters.name: messageKind
parameters.description: 0 text (default), 1 photo, 2 location. NULL → 0. Validated by HC6.ChatMessageKindError; a bad pairing → 2012.

parameters.name: replyToMessageId
parameters.description: The message this one quotes (E9.F1.S21). Kept only when it is a message of THIS thread (ThreadId match); otherwise silently cleared and the message sends without a quote.

rowsets.description: Returned alone, then RETURN, on: auth failure (from ValidateAppAuth); 2010 missing messageId/threadId/content (errorType 2); 2011 content over 4,000 (2); 2012 bad message kind (2); 2013 thread not open for the sender — 'You can't message <name>.' (3); 2014 unhandled error in the write transaction (5).

rowsets.name: Message
rowsets.description: On success: the message in the flutter_chat_core shape the chat page reads for every thread kind. One row.

columns.name: id
columns.description: UPPER(EventMessage.id). Uppercase on purpose — the client lowercases on arrival (HcId).

columns.name: type
columns.description: Always 'text' — even for a photo or location; messageKind carries the kind.

columns.name: text
columns.description: EventMessage.MessageContent — the raw content (text, photo URL or map link).

columns.name: sequenceCount
columns.description: EventMessage.MessageSequenceCount, assigned by HC.trgCreateSeqNum per ThreadId.

columns.name: canDelete
columns.description: Always 1 — it is the sender's own message.

rowsets.name: PushDetail
rowsets.description: On success, API ONLY (stripped before the reply): what the shim needs to build the push. One row. Inside the log-and-swallow TRY — absent, with rowsets 2–3, if that section fails (logged as 'Push plumbing failed in sendDirectMessage (message was sent)').

columns.name: MessageTitle
columns.description: The sender's DisplayName (a DM push is titled by who sent it).

rowsets.name: VisibleRecipients
rowsets.description: On success, API ONLY: the other party's live devices (removed 0, FcmToken present, LastLogin within 180 days, build >= HC6.MinBuildForDmPush()) when their FriendNotificationPreference for the thread is neither 2 (none) nor 3 (muted). Empty when it is 2 or 3, or they have no qualifying device. The sender's own devices are NOT included (unlike kennel/event/room sends).

columns.name: UserId
columns.description: Device.UserId — the other party's internal Hasher.id.

columns.name: BadgeTotal
columns.description: HC6.UserUnreadChatTotal for the recipient; NULL when the device's build is below HC6.MinBuildForIconBadge().

rowsets.name: SilentRecipients
rowsets.description: On success, API ONLY: the same devices when the other party's FriendNotificationPreference is 3 (muted the thread) — a data-only push so the badge moves. Same columns as rowset 2.

sideEffects: INSERT HC.EventMessage (EventId NULL, KennelId NULL, ThreadId = @threadId, MessageTitle '', MessageReleasabilityFlags 63, MessageType 0) — fires HC.trgCreateSeqNum (MessageSequenceCount per thread) and HC.trgEventMessageActivityCount (no-op: EventId NULL).
MERGE HC.EventMessageBadgeCounts keyed on (UserId, EventId NULL, KennelId NULL, ThreadId = @threadId, MessageType 0) — the sender's LastSequenceCount and LastReadAt move to the new message.
INSERT HC.ErrorLog on every refused path, in the write CATCH, and in the push-plumbing CATCH (swallowed).
The API shim pushes to rowsets 2–3; nothing is queued in the database.

codeSmells.issue: Refusal text can name a hasher who blocked the caller
codeSmells.detail: Lines 102–103 look up the other party's DisplayName from the caller's own HasherFriendMap row for the error text 'You can't message <name>.' — fine for a thread the caller is in. For a @threadId the caller has no row for, @otherName is NULL and the text says 'this hasher', so nothing leaks. Noted only because the lookup ignores Removed/Ignore on purpose; the message deliberately does not say WHY.

breakingChangeRules: Never remove a column from any rowset
Never change a sentinel value meaning
Never change errorType integer codes without updating all callers
